title: Implement a modular gradient descent optimizer suite in pure NumPy
brief:
In order to deeply understand optimizer mechanics before debugging large-scale distributed training runs, you are tasked with building a modular, object-oriented gradient descent optimizer framework in pure Python and NumPy from first principles.

Your library must support vanilla SGD, Polyak Heavy-Ball Momentum, RMSProp, Adam, and decoupled AdamW, along with gradient norm clipping and a cosine annealing learning rate scheduler.
deliverables: A clean BaseOptimizer abstract class with step(), zero_grad(), and parameter registration interfaces
Vectorized implementations of SGD with momentum (v_t = beta * v_{t-1} + lr * g_t)
Vectorized Adam optimizer with first and second moment moving averages, bias correction factors (1 - beta^t), and epsilon stability guards
Decoupled AdamW implementation demonstrating why direct weight decay differs from L2 gradient regularization in adaptive optimizers
A global gradient clipping utility that scales gradients down if the L2 norm exceeds a threshold (clip_grad_norm)
A benchmark script optimizing an ill-conditioned quadratic bowl and the 2D Rosenbrock banana valley, comparing convergence paths and step counts
